description:
Shell and pipeline cases: cooperative pipes, SIGPIPE, traps, jobs and sibling tool probes.

These were the harness's original built-in cases. `probe-tool` and `legacy-stdin` are fixtures
of the cooperative example; the oracle has neither, so their cases carry whole-result fixtures.

cases.name: input process substitution
cases.script: printf side-effect; cat <(echo input)

cases.name: output process substitution
cases.script: printf side-effect; echo output > >(cat)

cases.name: endless copy
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | cat | head -n 1

cases.name: multiple incremental filters
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | tr x y | grep y | sed s/y/z/ | cut -c1- | head -n 1

cases.name: early grep
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | grep -q x; echo status=$?

cases.name: early sed
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | sed 1q | cat

cases.name: early jq
cases.script: while :; do echo '{"x":"ø"}'; done | jq .x | head -n 1

cases.name: early xargs
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | xargs -n 1 echo | head -n 1

cases.name: tail from start
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | tail -n +2 | head -n 1

cases.name: subshell isolation
cases.script: v=outer; echo inner | { read v; echo "$v"; }; echo "$v"

cases.name: lastpipe
cases.script: shopt -s lastpipe; printf 'héllø\n' | read -N 2 v; echo "$v"

cases.name: success status array
cases.script: true | false | true; echo "$? ${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: pipefail
cases.script: set -o pipefail; true | false | true; echo "$? ${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: finite pipefail
cases.script: set -o pipefail; printf fresh | cat | cat; echo "status=$? ${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: early pipefail
cases.script: set -o pipefail; while :; do echo x; done | cat | head -n 1; echo "$? ${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

cases.name: functions and loops
cases.script: f() { while :; do echo x; done | cat; }; f | cat | head -n 1; echo after

cases.name: nested substitution
cases.script: echo "$(echo "$(echo x | cat)" | cat)"

cases.name: large substitution
cases.script: v=$(printf '%100000s\n' x | cat); echo ${#v}

cases.name: large record
cases.script: printf '%100000s\n' x | cat | head -c 10 | wc -c

cases.name: large here document
cases.script:
cat <<'EOF' | cat | head -c 10

EOF

cases.name: here string
cases.script: cat <<<hello | head -c 2

cases.name: sequential reads
cases.script: printf 'héllø\nsecond\n' | { read a; read b; echo "$a:$b"; }

cases.name: mapfile
cases.script: printf 'héllø\nsecond' | { mapfile -t a; printf '%s\n' "${a[@]}"; }

cases.name: redirected producer
cases.script: echo hi > /tmp/redirected | head -n 0; cat /tmp/redirected

cases.name: local stderr

cases.name: merged local stderr
cases.script: { echo out; echo err >&2; } 2>&1 | cat

cases.name: pipe ampersand precedence
cases.script: { echo out; echo err >&2; } 2>/tmp/error |& cat; cat /tmp/error

cases.name: command directories
cases.script: mkdir /tmp/a /tmp/b; (cd /tmp/a; echo data > local; cat local) | (cd /tmp/b; read v; echo "$v"; pwd); pwd

cases.name: unconsumed stdin
cases.script: printf 'b\na\n' >/tmp/input; while :; do echo x; done | sort /tmp/input | cat

cases.name: negative head count

b
c

cases.name: yielding timeout

cases.name: tail zero exits early

cases.name: foreground file follow

cases.name: formatted printf repeated

cases.name: pending tool and progressing consumer
cases.script: probe-tool delay | { read -t 0.01 v; echo before=$?; echo ready >/tmp/probe-peer; read v; echo "$v"; }

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: yielding tool input
cases.script: printf "%100000s\n" x | probe-tool input | head -c 10 | wc -c

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: tool context in nested substitution
cases.script: echo "$(probe-tool input <<<hello | cat)"

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: completion after reader exit then fresh input
cases.script: set -o pipefail; probe-tool delay | head -n 0; printf "status=%s pipes=%s\n" "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; cat /tmp/probe-completed; printf fresh | probe-tool input; echo done

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: ignored PIPE tool completion after reader exit
cases.script: trap '' PIPE; set -o pipefail; probe-tool delay | head -n 0; printf "status=%s pipes=%s\n" "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; cat /tmp/probe-completed; printf fresh | probe-tool input; echo done

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: tool named exit code
cases.script: probe-tool fail 2>/tmp/tool-error; echo status=$?; cat /tmp/tool-error

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: delayed completion stays command scoped
cases.script: { echo begin; probe-tool delay; echo survived >/tmp/tool-parent; } | { read v; sleep 0.01; echo "$v"; }; cat /tmp/probe-completed; cat /tmp/tool-parent; printf fresh | probe-tool input; echo done

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: tool failure after output preserves status
cases.script: set -o pipefail; probe-tool fail-output | cat; echo "status=$? ${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: unsupported workflows refuse immediately
cases.script: prompt-user question >/dev/null 2>&1; a=$?; confirm action >/dev/null 2>&1; b=$?; sudo true >/dev/null 2>&1; c=$?; if test "$a" -ne 0 && test "$b" -ne 0 && test "$c" -ne 0; then echo refused; else echo unexpected; fi

cases.name: following commands
cases.script: while :; do echo x; done | cat | head -n 1; printf 'fresh\n' | cat; echo after

cases.name: reader close preserves later effects
cases.script: { printf x; sleep 0.03; echo survived >/tmp/lifetime; echo diagnostic >&2; } | head -c 1; cat /tmp/lifetime

cases.name: failed builtin write kills only its stage
cases.script: set -o pipefail; { while :; do printf x; done; echo bad >/tmp/builtin-after; } | head -c 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; if test -e /tmp/builtin-after; then echo leaked; else echo absent; fi

cases.name: failed utility write leaves group alive
cases.script: printf '%100000s\n' x >/tmp/utility-input; { cat /tmp/utility-input; echo survived >/tmp/utility-after; } | head -c 1; cat /tmp/utility-after

cases.name: failed nested pipeline leaves group alive
cases.script: { while :; do echo x; done | cat; echo survived >/tmp/nested-after; } | head -n 1; cat /tmp/nested-after

cases.name: ignored PIPE is inherited
cases.script: trap '' PIPE; { while :; do echo x 2>/dev/null || break; done; echo continued >/tmp/ignored-after; } | head -n 1; cat /tmp/ignored-after

cases.name: caught PIPE preserves failed status
cases.script: { trap 'echo handler:$? >/tmp/caught-status' PIPE; while :; do echo x 2>/dev/null || break; done; echo continued >/tmp/caught-after; } | head -n 1; cat /tmp/caught-status; cat /tmp/caught-after

cases.name: caught SIGPIPE handler exits 23
cases.script: set -o pipefail; { trap 'echo handler:$? >/tmp/caught-exit; exit 23' SIGPIPE; while :; do echo x 2>/dev/null; done; } | head -n 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; cat /tmp/caught-exit

cases.name: numeric signal 13 handler exits 23
cases.script: set -o pipefail; { trap 'echo handler:$? >/tmp/caught-13; exit 23' 13; while :; do echo x 2>/dev/null; done; } | head -n 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; cat /tmp/caught-13

cases.name: reset PIPE restores default
cases.script: set -o pipefail; { trap 'echo bad >/tmp/reset-handler' PIPE; trap - PIPE; while :; do echo x; done; } | head -n 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; if test -e /tmp/reset-handler; then echo leaked; else echo reset; fi

cases.name: inherited caught PIPE is displayed but inert
cases.script: trap 'echo bad >/tmp/inherited-handler' PIPE; set -o pipefail; { trap -p PIPE >/tmp/inherited-display; while :; do echo x; done; } | head -n 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; cat /tmp/inherited-display; if test -e /tmp/inherited-handler; then echo leaked; else echo inert; fi

cases.name: function shares caught PIPE process
cases.script: { trap 'echo handler:$? >/tmp/function-handler' PIPE; f() { while :; do echo x 2>/dev/null || break; done; echo continued >/tmp/function-after; }; f; } | head -n 1; cat /tmp/function-handler; cat /tmp/function-after

cases.name: subshell resets caught PIPE
cases.script: { trap 'echo bad >/tmp/subshell-handler' PIPE; (while :; do echo x; done); printf 'sub=%s\n' "$?" >/tmp/subshell-status; echo continued >/tmp/subshell-after; } | head -n 1; cat /tmp/subshell-status; cat /tmp/subshell-after; if test -e /tmp/subshell-handler; then echo leaked; else echo inert; fi

cases.name: substitution has its own PIPE process
cases.script: trap 'echo bad >/tmp/substitution-handler' PIPE; value=$(while :; do echo x; done | head -n 1); printf '%s\n' "$value"; if test -e /tmp/substitution-handler; then echo leaked; else echo inert; fi

cases.name: lastpipe trap mutation persists
cases.script: shopt -s lastpipe; printf x | trap 'echo lastpipe' PIPE; trap -p PIPE

cases.name: oversized trap display drains asynchronously
cases.script: body=$(printf '%100000s' x); trap "$body" PIPE; trap -p PIPE | wc -c

cases.name: trap signal listing handles backpressure
cases.script: set -o pipefail; { for i in {1..10000}; do trap -l; echo; done; echo bad >/tmp/trap-list-after; } | cat | head -n 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; if test -e /tmp/trap-list-after; then echo leaked; else echo absent; fi

cases.name: PIPE handler recursion is suppressed
cases.script: set -o pipefail; ( { trap 'echo recurse 2>/dev/null; echo once >/tmp/pipe-once; exit 23' PIPE; while :; do echo x 2>/dev/null; done; } | head -n 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}" ) 2>/dev/null; cat /tmp/pipe-once

expected.reason: the synthetic SIGPIPE is not re-raised while its handler runs

cases.name: closed diagnostic stream keeps ignored status
cases.script: trap '' PIPE; { while :; do echo x 2>&-; rc=$?; if test "$rc" -ne 0; then echo "$rc" >/tmp/closed-status; break; fi; done; } | head -n 1; cat /tmp/closed-status

cases.name: closed diagnostic stream still delivers caught PIPE
cases.script: set -o pipefail; { trap 'echo handler:$? >/tmp/closed-handler; exit 23' PIPE; while :; do echo x 2>&1; done; } 2>&1 | head -c 1; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; cat /tmp/closed-handler

cases.name: PIPE handler precedes ERR and errexit
cases.script: set -o pipefail; { set -eE; trap 'touch /tmp/pipe-seen' PIPE; trap 'if test -e /tmp/pipe-seen; then touch /tmp/ordered; else touch /tmp/reversed; fi; if test -e /tmp/err-once; then touch /tmp/err-duplicate; else touch /tmp/err-once; fi' ERR; sleep 0.03; echo x 2>/dev/null; echo bad >/tmp/errexit-after; } | true; printf 'status=%s pipes=%s\n' "$?" "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; if test -e /tmp/pipe-seen; then echo pipe; else echo missing-pipe; fi; if test -e /tmp/ordered && test ! -e /tmp/reversed; then echo ordered; else echo reversed; fi; if test -e /tmp/err-once && test ! -e /tmp/err-duplicate; then echo once; else echo duplicate; fi; if test -e /tmp/errexit-after; then echo leaked; else echo absent; fi

stderr.text: synchronous stdin commands cannot consume cooperative pipes; use an async command with OpenFile::async_io()

expected.reason: legacy-stdin is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command
